The safety factor is widely used in aircraft design.
The traditional safety factor for metallic structures is 1.5.
Composite materials have a two-parameter Weibull distribution or normal distribution.
The coefficient of variation of the experimental results for composite materials is very large.
The recommended value of the safety factor for composite structures relative to the 1.5 safety factor for metallic structures is about 2.0.
The shape parameter of the Weibull distribution for composite materials is usually about 10.
The factor of safety for composite materials when the shape parameter is 10 is about 2.
The safety factor increases as the Weibull parameter decreases.
The recommended value of the safety factor for loads in composite structures is approximately the same as for metallic structures.
The coefficient of variation of the materials used in conventional metallic structures is 0.03.
The recommended value of the safety factor for strength in composite structures is about 1.1.
Reducing the scatter of materials used in composite structures can increase the reliability or decrease the factor of safety at a given reliability.
The method presented in the paper for determining the safety factor for composite structures is a technique based on structural system reliability.
The formula for determining the safety factor for composite structures is f = 1 + p_v + v^2 / (2 * v).
The safety factor should consider not only the scatter of strength and exceptionally large loads but also the failure mechanism and failure modes of the composite structures.
The safety factor for composite structures can be determined using the Weibull distribution of composite materials and the loads applied to the structures.
